calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building has one or two lawful parking spaces on a driveway in the front yard, the ban on street yard parking in 10.5.80.10(3) does not apply while those spaces remain.

On a lot with a lawfully existing driveway wider than 10.5.100.1(1) allows that leads to only one parking space behind the front main wall, two parking spaces may be side by side on the driveway in the front yard if the driveway width does not exceed 6.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the as-built driveway width and parking facts.

calculation_handling.description: If required parking spaces cannot be located where the by-law requires on a lawfully existing lot with a lawfully existing building, they may be entirely or partly in the front yard if approved under the City of Toronto Act, 2006.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on an approval under the City of Toronto Act, 2006.

10.5.80.11(1).explanation: A lawfully existing building with one or two lawful driveway parking spaces in the front yard is exempt from the street yard parking ban in 10.5.80.10(3) for as long as those spaces remain.

10.5.80.11(2).explanation: A lawfully existing detached or semi-detached house with a lawfully existing driveway wider than 10.5.100.1(1) allows, leading to one parking space behind the front main wall, may have two side-by-side front yard spaces on that driveway if it is no wider than 6.0 m.

10.5.80.11(3).explanation: If a lawfully existing lot and building cannot place required parking where the by-law requires, the spaces may be wholly or partly in the front yard with approval under the City of Toronto Act, 2006.
